summary: Edeltraud Harzer is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned degrees from Charles University and the University of Washington, and studied under Sri Narayana Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas.

Edgar Howard Sturtevant (1875–1952) was a linguist who studied at Illinois College, Indiana University, and the University of Chicago under Carl Darling Buck. He held faculty posts at Indiana, Maryville, Missouri, Columbia (1907–1920), and Yale (1923–1943).

Edgar Polomé (1920–2000) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned degrees from the Université libre de Bruxelles and KU Leuven, studying under Étienne Lamotte. He taught at the University of Lubumbashi (1956–1960) and directed at the University of Texas (1961–1997).

Edgar Thurston (1855–1935) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Eton and King's College London, he served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1885–1908), taught anatomy at Madras Medical College, and was Superintendent of Ethnography for Madras Presidency.

Edgard Blochet (1870–1937) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at the EPHE and INALCO under James Darmesteter, then served as teacher at the EPHE and librarian at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Edith Frances Claflin (1875–1953) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She earned degrees from Radcliffe College and Bryn Mawr College, then headed the Greek Department at Choate Rosemary Hall (1916–1933) and lectured at Barnard College (1936–1945).

Edith Ludowyk-Gyömrői (1896–1987) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Ceylon, where she studied under G. P. Malalasekera from around 1941 to 1944.

Edith Tóth (1932–1965) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. She studied under Lajos Ligeti, János Harmatta, and László Gaál, and served as Keeper of the Indian collection at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts (ca. 1958–1965).

Edith Wyschogrod (1930–2009) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from Hunter College and her Ph.D. from Columbia University, serving as J. Newton Rayzor Professor at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.
Edmond Yee (b. 1938) is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology. Around 1985, he served as a faculty member at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.

Edmund Charles Cox (1856–1935) was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He received his education at Marlborough College from around 1869 to 1874 and at Trinity College, Cambridge from around 1874 to 1877.

Edmund Hardy (1852–1904) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg (under Kuno Fischer), and Freiburg, he held posts at the universities of Freiburg (1885–1893), Fribourg (1894–1898), and Würzburg (ca. 1898–1904).

Edmund Henderson Hunt (1874–1952) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Harrow School and Balliol College, Oxford, and later served as Chief Medical Officer for the Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway from around 1904 to 1931.

Edmund Husserl (1859–1938) was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt, Berlin, Vienna, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (ca. 1887–1901), the University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and the University of Freiburg (1916–1928).

Edmund Kleinhans (1870–1934) was a linguist. He studied at the University of Innsbruck from around 1889 to 1895 under Friedrich Stolz, and also pursued studies at the University of Leipzig from 1892 to 1893 under Karl Brugmann.

Edmund Leach (1910–1989) worked in religious studies. He studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and the LSE under Alfred Radcliffe-Brown and Bronisław Malinowski. He held posts at the LSE, the University of Cambridge, and served as Provost of King's College, Cambridge.

Edmund Martin Küttler (1884–1964) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Vienna under Leopold von Schroeder, Berlin, and Graz. He served at the Institut für Kulturforschung, Masaryk University, and as Director of the Moravian Museum until 1945.

Edmund Nathaniel Snyder (d. 1896) was an Indologist educated at Harvard, Berlin (under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg), and Leipzig. He taught Latin at Vassar College in 1890 and served as Professor of German and French at University School.
Edmund Stengel studied under Nikolaus Delius and Friedrich Christian Diez between approximately 1865 and 1868.

Edmund W. Smith (1858–1901) was an archaeologist and Indologist. In 1886, he served as Assistant Archaeological Surveyor for the North-West Provinces and Oudh with the Archaeological Survey of India, and became Curator at the State Museum, Lucknow, in 1898.
